subject: Post-demo: pricing breakdown & context-size follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@veridianlabs.com>, Michael Ortiz <michael.ortiz@veridianlabs.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood demo — quick recap + asks on token volumes/context

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the time. Short recap and a few very specific asks so we can put together a tailored pricing and capacity proposal.

Recap (2 min):
- Use case: product search + conversational help across product catalog + automated summaries for sales ops.
- Peak: internal estimate ~1.2M user queries/month, most are short Q&A but ~10-15% are context-heavy (order history + product descriptions + up to 50 item vectors).
- Session pattern: avg 1.6 requests/session; expected growth to 2.1 next quarter.

Asks (what we need to price accurately):
1) Typical per-interaction token breakdown: avg prompt tokens and avg completion tokens (if you can share a sample distribution that’s ideal).
2) How many sessions/queries per month do you expect in year-1 vs year-2? (ballpark is fine).
3) Context window needs: are any flows expected to need 32k or 128k context, or will 8k suffice for nearly all production traffic?
4) Target unit economics: do you have a target spend per 1M tokens or monthly budget range we should adhere to?

Next steps: If you can reply with (1)-(4) today or tomorrow, I’ll share a 1M-token cost breakdown across 8k/32k/128k profiles plus an estimated monthly cost using your volumes. Attached: demo recording and a sample pricing workbook.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: demo-recording-20260518.mp4 (recording, 75MB)
Attachment: redwood-pricing-1M-breakdown.xlsx (workbook)
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@veridianlabs.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Ortiz <michael.ortiz@veridianlabs.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 15:43:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — quick recap + asks on token volumes/context

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below (we can follow up with logs if needed):

1) Token profile (approx averages across current pilot):
- Short intent queries (60%): prompt ~120 tokens, completion ~60 tokens
- Conversational product help (25%): prompt ~420 tokens, completion ~300 tokens
- Deep summaries / multi-doc concat (15%): prompt ~3,400 tokens, completion ~400–800 tokens depending on summary length

2) Volumes: current pilot ~150k queries/month. Ramp plan: 1.0M qtrs 3–4 2026 (conservative), 1.8M by mid-2027.

3) Context window: most flows today fit within 8k, but the deep summary flow sometimes needs 32k for multi-doc concatenation. We do not expect regular 128k usage; consider it occasional for large quarterly reports (maybe <1% of traffic).

4) Budget target: we’re looking for a predictable < $10k/month for pilot; for production scale we have a target blended unit cost around $300–700 per 1M tokens (very preliminary).

Happy to share a small sample of anonymized logs if that helps with finer-grain pricing.

— Sophie
Head of Product | Veridian Labs
Sophie.Lang@veridianlabs.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@veridianlabs.com>, Michael Ortiz <michael.ortiz@veridianlabs.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — quick recap + asks on token volumes/context

Thanks Sophie — this is super helpful. I did a quick back-of-envelope to show how we’d map that profile to expected monthly token volumes and a 1M-token cost example so we can discuss unit economics. See bullets below and I attached the detailed workbook.

Assumptions (from your share):
- Use-case mix = 60% short intent, 25% conv help, 15% deep summaries
- Ramp to Year-1 steady state: 1.0M queries/month (we’ll also show 1.8M scenario in the workbook)

Average tokens per interaction (weighted):
- prompt avg = (0.6*120) + (0.25*420) + (0.15*3400) = 72 + 105 + 510 = 687 prompt tokens avg
- completion avg = (0.6*60) + (0.25*300) + (0.15*600) = 36 + 75 + 90 = 201 completion tokens avg
- total = 888 tokens per interaction on average

Monthly tokens at 1.0M queries: ~888M tokens/month total (prompt+completion).

Costing examples (illustrative):
- If target is $300 per 1M tokens, monthly cost ~ $266.4k (888 * $300) — not aligned with your stated target but useful to compare.
- At $700 per 1M tokens, monthly cost ~ $621.6k

8k vs 32k vs 128k implications:
- Most traffic fits 8k -> we can serve widely optimized kernels and aggressive batching.
- The deep summary 15% that approaches 3.4k prompt tokens fits 8k today; the multi-doc concatenation to 32k would increase average prompt tokens for that subset and reduce batching efficiency. Expect ~10–25% per-token cost uplift when switching that flow to 32k model variants due to lower throughput and larger memory footprint (workbook has model-specific numbers).
- 128k would be niche and priced as specialized capacity — we model it as +2x the per-token unit cost baseline for those requests since they consume GPU memory and reduce batching by design.

Questions for you so we can finalize a tailored proposal:
- Can you share a sample of 1–2k anonymized interactions so we can compute exact distributions?
- Is the $300–700/1M an internal target or a hard budget cap for year-1 production?
- For the deep-summary flows, do they need real-time sub-second latency or is 2–5s acceptable (affects routing to cheaper vs faster capacity)?

I’ll follow up with a concise pricing sheet across three scenarios (pilot, 1M q/mo, 1.8M q/mo) and three context profiles (8k-only, hybrid 8k+32k, occasional 128k). Expect that in ~24 hours once we get the sample logs.

Best,
Jordan

Attachment: redwood-pricing-1M-breakdown.xlsx (calcs for 8k/32k/128k)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — pricing breakdown & context-size follow-up

Sophie — quick note from infra/architecture side: if you plan to push the multi-doc concat to 32k for a significant fraction of requests we recommend:
- Start with a hybrid approach (8k default, 32k route for the summary pipeline) and instrument prefix caching aggressively to reduce repeated tokens.
- Consider offloading long-document pre-processing (chunking + embeddings) into a cheaper batch pipeline; then use the 32k window only for final assembly/summary. That pattern typically cuts 32k exposure by ~60% in our customers.

We’ll include capacity and autoscaling options in the pricing sheet — including a Dedicated reserved pool option that can dramatically reduce per-token effective cost if you commit baseline QPS.

Small ask: please upload a 48–72 hour sample of anonymized events to the Drive link Jordan shared so we can run exact sims.

— Vivek
Director, Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference
